groups.title: Soft Capsule (A80800ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to improve physical tiredness, as a tonic, and for the supply of vitamin B1 during and after illness.
groups.usage: Children aged 15 years and older and adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If nausea, vomiting, loose stools, rash or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral Suspension (227730ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to remove bubbles in the bowel during gastroscopy, to remove gas in the bowel during abdominal X-ray examination, and to improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract (a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, aerophagia and the like).
groups.usage: Adults: to remove bubbles in the bowel for gastroscopy, take 40 to 80 mg with about 10 mL of water 15 to 40 minutes before the examination. To remove gas in the bowel for abdominal X-ray examination, take 40 to 80 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or between meals, starting 3 to 4 days before the examination. To improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract, take 40 to 80 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or at bedtime. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

It must be given with care to people who are sensitive, and to people who are sensitive to sulfites.

Shake it well before use.

Occasionally loose stools, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, nausea, a feeling of heaviness in the abdomen or loss of appetite, and rarely headache may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Removal of bubbles or gas in the bowel for gastroscopy and abdominal X-ray, and abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract

groups.title: Tablet (D12500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth and eye membranes), asthma, liver function disorder (general lassitude, jaundice with yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (257100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for paroxysmal pain of gastrointestinal disease and for functional disturbance and spasmodic pain of the biliary system, the urinary system and the female reproductive system, including dysmenorrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Do not exceed a maximum of 6 tablets in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have had hypersensitivity to it (rash, red spots, itching, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips); if you have had asthma caused by another cold medicine or antipyretic analgesic; if you have severe kidney impairment or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency; if you have glaucoma or prostatic hyperplasia; if you have pyloric stenosis or paralytic intestinal obstruction; if you have muscle weakness or megacolon; if you have tachyarrhythmia; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver function disturbance; if you have Gilbert's syndrome (Meulengracht's disease); if you have severe heart disease, coronary insufficiency or heart failure; or if you are pregnant (especially within the first 3 months of pregnancy) or breast-feeding.

It is not desirable to give this medicine to children. Take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, an antiepileptic or rifampicin. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antihistamine, quinidine, amantadine, disopyramide, an antidopaminergic medicine such as metoclopramide, a beta agonist, propantheline, chloramphenicol, an oral anticoagulant, zidovudine or flucloxacillin.

Thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, cyanosis, leukopenia, pancytopenia, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, thirst, difficulty passing urine, dilated pupils, ciliary muscle paralysis, flushing, dizziness, anxiety, excitement, hallucination, orthostatic low blood pressure, rash, rapid heartbeat, abnormally high body temperature or high anion gap metabolic acidosis may occur.

If Quincke's oedema, difficulty breathing, sweating, nausea, a fall in blood pressure, shock, reddening of the skin, skin symptoms such as rash, urticaria, swelling (of the throat, eyelids, lips and the like) or chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and breathlessness, or rash with high fever, burn-like blisters or asthma occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Paroxysmal pain of gastrointestinal disease and functional disturbance and spasmodic pain of the biliary, urinary and female reproductive systems, including period pain

groups.title: Soft Capsule (D21900ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for pain relief in headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, period pain and pain from injury, and for reducing fever with chills.
groups.usage: Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 to 2 capsules per dose. Take it 1 to 3 times in 1 day, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours, and avoid taking it on an empty stomach.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should use ibuprofen only after careful consideration and should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day). Also, if a person with cardiovascular risk factors (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes or smoking) needs high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), consider this carefully before starting long-term treatment. Clinical studies have shown that use of high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) may slightly increase the risk of arterial thrombotic events (myocardial infarction or stroke).

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or are not taking in fluid; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, a diuretic or low-dose aspirin. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

groups.title: Syrup (180830ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation (chronic constipation, constipation in babies, young children and children, and constipation after childbirth).
groups.usage: For chronic constipation, take it before breakfast. Adults: take 15 to 30 mL in 1 day by mouth before breakfast for the first 2 to 3 days, then continue with 10 to 15 mL in 1 day. In severe cases up to 45 mL may be given. Ages 7 years to 14 years: take 15 mL in 1 day for the first 2 to 3 days, then continue with 10 mL in 1 day. Ages 1 year to 6 years: take 5 to 10 mL in 1 day. Under 12 months of age: take 5 mL in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease); if you have gastrointestinal obstruction; if you have abdominal pain of unknown cause; if you are on a low-galactose diet (galactosaemia); if you have, or are at risk of, perforation of the digestive tract; if you have hypersensitivity to it; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a baby, a young child or a child; if you are an older person; if you have diabetes or fructose intolerance; if you have a fluid or electrolyte imbalance; if you have acute gastritis; or if the constipation is chronic.

If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist. If loose stools or diarrhoea occurs, reduce the dose or stop taking it.

While you are taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor such as acarbose, a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a diuretic, a corticoid, amphotericin B, a cardiac glycoside or an antacid.

If digestive adverse reactions (belching, cramping abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea) or, occasionally, bowel sounds, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea or vomiting occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Constipation, including chronic constipation, constipation in babies and children, and constipation after childbirth

groups.title: Tablet (130501ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria and itching of the skin, and, in combination with a topical hydrocortisone preparation, for eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 6 years and older: take 1 tablet (10 mg), 1 time in 1 day, before bedtime; for people sensitive to adverse reactions, take 1/2 tablet (5 mg) per dose in the morning and in the evening as divided doses. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. In people with kidney impairment the dosing interval must be adjusted to kidney function, and in children with kidney impairment the dose must be adjusted individually according to renal clearance and body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.
groups.caution:
This medicine is not for people with hypersensitivity to it or to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives, or for people with renal failure (creatinine clearance below 10 mL/min).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you have kidney impairment or liver impairment; if you are an older person; if you have epilepsy or a risk of seizures; or if you have a predisposing factor for urinary retention (spinal cord lesion, prostatic hyperplasia).

Do not take it together with theophylline or ritonavir. Do not take it together with a large amount of alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: drowsiness, headache; occasionally lassitude, numbness, weakness, agitation, abnormal sensation, thirst, dry lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, palpitations, vasculitis, reduced white blood cells, reduced neutrophils, increased lymphocytes, increased eosinophils, swelling, itching, rash, liver function disturbance such as raised AST, ALT, ALP, total bilirubin, gamma-GTP or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, raised BUN, sugar in the urine, blood in the urine or chest pain; rarely mild and temporary listlessness, fatigue, dizziness, a heavy head, excitement, convulsions, movement disorder, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucination, insomnia, tic disorder, loss of memory, memory disturbance, suicidal ideation, nightmares, vomiting, gastrointestinal disturbance, inflammation of the lips, taste disturbance, increased appetite, rapid heartbeat, arrhythmia, raised blood pressure, increased monocytes, increased platelets, reduced platelets, photosensitivity, hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock, urticaria, angioneurotic oedema, fixed drug eruption, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of eye accommodation, oculogyric crisis, vertigo, difficulty passing urine, bed-wetting, urinary retention, joint pain, muscle pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing disturbance, visual disturbance, menstrual disturbance, ringing in the ears, rhinitis or weight gain.

Itching and urticaria may appear after this medicine is stopped.

groups.title: Capsule (461134ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to regulate the bowel by normalising the intestinal flora and to improve the symptoms of diarrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 4 capsules in 1 day, swallowing them whole with water without opening them.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if you are pregnant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

To make up for the fluid lost through diarrhoea, rehydrate by drinking plenty of drinks containing salt or sugar.

If you keep eating while you have diarrhoea, do not take certain foods, especially raw food, fruit, vegetables, spicy food and frozen food or drinks. Eat mainly cooked meat and rice.

If symptoms do not improve after taking it for 2 days, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (142301ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you are breast-feeding; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation during earlier treatment with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure; if you have high blood pressure; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you are in early or mid pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have had major surgery with blood loss; or if you have a blood clotting disorder or are being given an anticoagulant.

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate (15 mg a week or more) used as cancer treatment. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (trimethoprim, heparin and the like), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, or if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely triggering of an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; rarely jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbance such as scotoma or dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; rarely mental disturbance, agitation, excitement, disorientation or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral oedema, acute pulmonary oedema, fluid retention, high blood pressure, heart failure or reduced fertility in women; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.

groups.title: Oral Solution (D07600ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 bottle per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals. Leave an interval of 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 2 years of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, swelling or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain, an ulcer or a bleeding problem; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a potassium-containing preparation, a liquorice-containing preparation, a preparation containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, a loop diuretic (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or a thiazide diuretic (trichlormethiazide), a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing and the like), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (with high fever and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth and eye membranes), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever, reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, raised blood pressure, headache or myopathy (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (402300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of sneezing, runny nose, blocked nose and watering eyes caused by a cold or by allergic and vasomotor rhinitis, and of nasal congestion caused by sinusitis.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet every 4 hours, and do not exceed 6 tablets in 24 hours. Children aged 6 years to under 12 years: take 1/2 tablet every 4 hours, and do not exceed 3 tablets in 24 hours. For children under 6 years of age, follow the instructions of a doctor.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to amine sympathomimetics or antihistamines; if you have an idiosyncratic constitution; if you are breast-feeding; if you have severe high blood pressure or severe coronary artery disease; if you are being treated with an MAO inhibitor; if you have narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention, peptic ulcer, asthma, emphysema or chronic lung disease; if you are short of breath or have difficulty breathing; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have difficulty breathing such as chronic bronchitis, heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid disease, diabetes, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

If symptoms do not improve within 7 days, or if a high fever occurs at the same time, consult a doctor. Take care when driving or operating machinery after taking it.

Do not use it together with an MAO inhibitor, a sedative or a tranquilliser. Avoid alcoholic drinks while taking it.

If fear, anxiety, tension, tremor, weakness, pallor, difficulty breathing, difficulty passing urine, insomnia, hallucination, convulsions, central nervous system depression, arrhythmia, dizziness, cardiovascular collapse with low blood pressure, rapid heartbeat, palpitations, headache, nausea, thirst, weakness, loss of appetite, vomiting, nervousness, excessive urine volume, heartburn, double vision, difficulty passing urine, drowsiness, excitement or, rarely, dermatitis occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.
